question: Gig apps sell the freedom to choose your hours. In an experiment, how much pay would job seekers give up for it?
answer: Almost nothing, on average. Mas and Pallais offered call-centre job applicants schedules at different wages. Most would pay little to set their own hours, yet the average applicant would forgo 20% of pay to avoid a schedule the employer could change at short notice. People pay to escape someone else's calendar, not to own one.
move: Ask what people pay to avoid something, not only to get it.
reference: Mas & Pallais, Valuing Alternative Work Arrangements, American Economic Review, 2017
